_about: Early human spread layer, compiled for History Globe from widely cited published estimates. Dates are approximate and several are debated; t is an astronomical year (1950 - years before present). Routes are schematic, not exact paths.

sites.name: Jebel Irhoud
sites.note: Oldest known Homo sapiens fossils, in Morocco: our species was already spread across Africa.

sites.name: Florisbad skull
sites.note: Early Homo sapiens or close relative in southern Africa.

sites.name: Omo Kibish
sites.note: Omo I, among the oldest anatomically modern human remains, in Ethiopia.

sites.name: Misliya Cave
sites.note: A modern human jaw in Israel: an early, short-lived venture out of Africa.

sites.name: Skhul and Qafzeh
sites.note: Early modern humans in the Levant, alongside Neanderthals nearby.

sites.name: Blombos Cave
sites.note: Engraved ochre and shell beads: some of the earliest symbolic art.

sites.name: Toba eruption
sites.note: One of the largest known volcanic eruptions; its effect on early humans is debated.

sites.name: Madjedbebe
sites.note: Possibly the oldest evidence of people in Australia.

sites.name: Bacho Kiro Cave
sites.note: Among the earliest Homo sapiens in Europe, in Bulgaria.

sites.name: Lake Mungo
sites.note: Mungo Man and Mungo Lady: Australia's oldest known human remains.

sites.name: Neanderthals fade out
sites.note: Neanderthals disappear (Gorham's Cave, Gibraltar, is among their last sites); many people today carry some of their DNA.

sites.name: Tianyuan Cave
sites.note: One of the oldest modern humans in East Asia, near Beijing.

sites.name: Chauvet Cave
sites.note: Painted lions, horses and rhinos in southern France.

sites.name: Yana Rhinoceros Horn Site
sites.note: People living far above the Arctic Circle in Siberia.

sites.name: White Sands footprints
sites.note: Human footprints in New Mexico that may push the peopling of the Americas back to the Ice Age.

sites.name: Monte Verde
sites.note: A settlement in southern Chile, far down the Americas.

sites.name: Clovis
sites.note: Clovis spear points spread across North America.

sites.name: Göbekli Tepe
sites.note: Monumental stone enclosures built by hunter-gatherers, before farming took hold.

sites.name: Jericho
sites.note: One of the oldest continuously settled places, with early farming.

sites.name: Lapita
sites.note: Lapita seafarers begin settling the remote Pacific islands.

sites.name: Madagascar settled
sites.note: Austronesian sailors from Borneo reach Madagascar.

sites.name: Hawaii settled
sites.note: Polynesian voyagers reach Hawaii.

sites.name: Rapa Nui settled
sites.note: Polynesians reach Easter Island.

sites.name: New Zealand settled
sites.note: The last major land mass to be settled by people.

routes.label: Main dispersal out of Africa (southern route)
Crossing to Sahul (Australia and New Guinea)
